cohort: 120 pregnant women (60 in the study group receiving continuous CTG monitoring and 60 in the control group) divided into low-risk and high-risk pregnancies.
finding: Continuous CTG monitoring in high-risk pregnancies was associated with improved Apgar scores at one minute and reduced total maternal complications during labor, while in low-risk pregnancies it led to increased instrumental delivery and cesarean section rates.
followup_time: Assessed at birth (Apgar scores at 1 and 5 minutes) and during labor.
